summary: Since 1892 Berea College in Kentucky has charged no tuition to any student it admits. International students go further: financial aid and scholarships cover 100% of tuition, housing, food and fees, and a campus job pays for personal expenses.
covers: All admitted international students receive aid and scholarships covering 100% of tuition, housing, food and fees.
Everyone works on campus through the Work Program — at least 10 hours a week, and most international students work 15–20 hours — earning over $2,000 during the school year for personal costs.
Summer jobs are available to international students on campus.
No bank statements are needed with the International Financial Questionnaire.
eligibility: International first-year applicants with strong academic records who can show English ability through TOEFL (68 iBT), IELTS (6.0 overall, 5 in each band), Duolingo (95), SAT (980) or ACT (19), taken within the last two years.
Berea serves students with limited financial means; admission is competitive and places for international students are limited.
how_to_apply: Apply online through Berea's admissions portal before the international deadline of 30 November.
Submit transcripts, test scores, recommendations and the International Financial Questionnaire.
If admitted, pay the $2,200 enrolment deposit — Berea can adjust aid if this is a genuine hardship.
Apply for your US student visa (F-1) with the I-20 Berea issues.
watch_out: The international deadline (30 November) is earlier than many US regular deadlines.
The Work Program is compulsory and part of the education — plan for 10–20 hours of work each week.
Berea is a small college in rural Kentucky; make sure the setting suits you.
